chapters.title: IN WHICH PHILEAS FOGG AND PASSEPARTOUT ACCEPT EACH OTHER, THE ONE AS MASTER, THE OTHER AS MAN

en.hover: Phileas Fogg, an enigmatic and precise English gentleman, hires a new French servant named Jean Passepartout to maintain his strictly regimented household.
en.detail: Mr. Phileas Fogg is an eccentric, extremely punctual, and wealthy member of the Reform Club in London. He lives a solitary and meticulously routine life at his home in Saville Row. Having dismissed his previous servant for bringing shaving water at the wrong temperature, Fogg interviews and hires Jean Passepartout, a Frenchman seeking a quiet life. Fogg then departs for his club exactly on schedule.

tracks.evidence: Phileas Fogg was seated squarely in his armchair
Passepartout remained alone in the house in Saville Row.

chapters.title: IN WHICH PASSEPARTOUT IS CONVINCED THAT HE HAS AT LAST FOUND HIS IDEAL

en.hover: Left alone in the house at Saville Row, Passepartout explores his new quarters and happily embraces the strict, orderly routine required by his master.
en.detail: Passepartout reflects on his new employer, Phileas Fogg, comparing the gentleman's extreme composure to a precise machine or a wax figure. Upon exploring the mansion at Saville Row, Passepartout is delighted by its comfort and the meticulous daily schedule laid out for him. After serving unpredictable masters in the past, he feels he has finally found the tranquil, predictable domestic life he desires.

tracks.evidence: At half-past eleven, then, Passepartout found himself alone in the house in Saville Row.

chapters.title: IN WHICH A CONVERSATION TAKES PLACE WHICH SEEMS LIKELY TO COST PHILEAS FOGG DEAR

en.hover: At the Reform Club, Phileas Fogg wagers twenty thousand pounds that he can travel around the world in eighty days, departing that very evening.
en.detail: Phileas Fogg arrives at the Reform Club and joins his usual whist partners. The men discuss a recent theft of fifty-five thousand pounds from the Bank of England and the likelihood of the culprit's escape. Fogg argues that the world has grown smaller and wagers twenty thousand pounds that he can circumnavigate the globe in eighty days. Despite his friends' doubts, Fogg pledges to depart for Dover that same evening and return by December 21st.

tracks.evidence: reached the Reform Club, an imposing edifice in Pall Mall

chapters.title: IN WHICH PHILEAS FOGG ASTOUNDS PASSEPARTOUT, HIS SERVANT

en.hover: Phileas Fogg stuns Passepartout by announcing their immediate departure to travel around the world in eighty days, boarding a train that very evening.
en.detail: Returning home earlier than usual, Phileas Fogg shocks his new servant, Passepartout, with the news that they are leaving for a journey around the world. Packing only a carpet-bag containing twenty thousand pounds, they rush to Charing Cross station. After Fogg gives his whist winnings to a beggar and bids his Reform Club friends farewell, the two depart by train.

tracks.evidence:
Just as the train was whirling through Sydenham, Passepartout suddenly uttered a cry of despair.

“What’s the matter?” asked Mr. Fogg.
Just as the train was whirling through Sydenham, Passepartout suddenly uttered a cry of despair.

chapters.title: IN WHICH A NEW SPECIES OF FUNDS, UNKNOWN TO THE MONEYED MEN, APPEARS ON 'CHANGE

en.hover: Fogg's wager sparks nationwide debate and betting, which turns against him entirely when a police telegram accuses him of the bank robbery.
en.detail: Phileas Fogg's departure becomes a national sensation, sparking intense debate, newspaper articles, and financial speculation across England. A highly critical article from the Royal Geographical Society causes his betting odds to plummet, leaving the elderly Lord Albemarle as his only backer. Public opinion collapses completely when the commissioner of police receives a telegram from Detective Fix in Suez, identifying Fogg as the bank robber.

chapters.title: IN WHICH FIX, THE DETECTIVE, BETRAYS A VERY NATURAL IMPATIENCE

en.hover: At Suez, Detective Fix awaits the steamer Mongolia, hoping to catch the bank robber, and is soon approached by a passenger with a familiar passport.
en.detail: Detective Fix and the British consul pace the wharves at Suez, anticipating the arrival of the steamer Mongolia. Fix explains his strategy for identifying the bank robber and firmly believes the suspect will pass through Suez. Once the ship arrives ahead of schedule, a passenger approaches Fix to ask for the consulate, handing over a passport that perfectly matches the description of the wanted man.

schedule.detail: in advance of the time required

tracks.evidence: This was Fix, one of the detectives

chapters.title: WHICH ONCE MORE DEMONSTRATES THE USELESSNESS OF PASSPORTS AS AIDS TO DETECTIVES

en.hover: Phileas Fogg and Passepartout visit the consul's office in Suez for a passport visa, unwittingly being scrutinized by Detective Fix.
en.detail: Detective Fix rushes to the British consul at Suez to explain his suspicions about the bank robber. Shortly after, Phileas Fogg and Passepartout arrive to have Fogg's passport visaed. Although the consul sees nothing amiss, Fix is determined to investigate further. Fogg returns to his cabin on the Mongolia and methodically logs his travel time, noting he is exactly on schedule.

schedule.detail: neither gained nor lost

tracks.evidence: went off to the ‘Mongolia’ in a boat
repaired to the quay, gave some orders to Passepartout

chapters.title: IN WHICH PASSEPARTOUT TALKS RATHER MORE, PERHAPS, THAN IS PRUDENT

en.hover: Detective Fix subtly interrogates an unsuspecting Passepartout, confirming his suspicions about Fogg, and subsequently boards the Mongolia in pursuit.
en.detail: On the quay at Suez, Detective Fix befriends Passepartout and pumps him for information. Hearing about Phileas Fogg's sudden departure from London, his large stash of brand new banknotes, and his supposed eighty-day journey around the world, Fix is entirely convinced Fogg is the bank robber. Fix wires London for an arrest warrant to be sent to Bombay, takes leave of the consul, and boards the Mongolia.

tracks.evidence: Passepartout and he had now reached the shop, where Fix left his companion
A quarter of an hour later found Fix, with a small bag in his hand, proceeding on board the “Mongolia;”

chapters.title: IN WHICH THE RED SEA AND THE INDIAN OCEAN PROVE PROPITIOUS TO THE DESIGNS OF PHILEAS FOGG

en.hover: Phileas Fogg and Passepartout travel aboard the Mongolia to Bombay, where Fogg plays whist and Fix subtly befriends Passepartout.
en.detail: Aboard the steamer Mongolia, Phileas Fogg remains indifferent to the sights of the Red Sea and Indian Ocean, occupying himself entirely with playing whist. Meanwhile, Detective Fix subtly befriends Passepartout to glean information without revealing his true identity. The ship makes excellent time, and Fogg arrives in Bombay two days ahead of schedule.

schedule.detail: gain of two days

tracks.evidence: Mr. Fogg and his servant went ashore at Aden to have the passport again visaed
Mr. Fogg and his servant went ashore at Aden
Fix, unobserved, followed them.

chapters.title: IN WHICH PASSEPARTOUT IS ONLY TOO GLAD TO GET OFF WITH THE LOSS OF HIS SHOES

en.hover: In Bombay, Fogg prepares to leave for Calcutta immediately, while Passepartout accidentally offends priests in a pagoda and narrowly escapes, losing his shoes.
en.detail: Upon arriving in Bombay, Phileas Fogg secures his passport and dines at the railway station, intending to depart for Calcutta that evening. Detective Fix tries but fails to get a local arrest warrant. Meanwhile, Passepartout wanders the city and naively enters a sacred pagoda without removing his shoes. He is attacked by priests but escapes to the station just in time, an incident Fix plans to use to detain Fogg.

tracks.evidence: Mr. Fogg, after bidding good-bye to his whist partners, left the steamer
Passepartout, however, had no sooner heard his master’s orders on leaving the “Mongolia”
Fix, who had followed Mr. Fogg to the station... was there, upon the platform.

chapters.title: IN WHICH PHILEAS FOGG SECURES A CURIOUS MEANS OF CONVEYANCE AT A FABULOUS PRICE

en.hover: The train journey across India stops abruptly at an unfinished section of track, prompting Phileas Fogg to purchase an elephant to continue.
en.detail: Phileas Fogg, Passepartout, and Sir Francis Cromarty travel by train across the Indian peninsula, passing dense forests and historic regions. The journey is abruptly halted at the hamlet of Kholby because the railway line is unfinished, despite newspaper reports to the contrary. Remaining calm, Fogg searches the village for alternative transport and ultimately purchases a half-domesticated elephant named Kiouni for the exorbitant sum of two thousand pounds to carry them to Allahabad.

schedule.detail: gained two days

tracks.evidence: An hour after leaving Bombay the train had passed the viaducts
An hour after leaving Bombay the train had passed the viaducts

chapters.title: IN WHICH PHILEAS FOGG AND HIS COMPANIONS VENTURE ACROSS THE INDIAN FORESTS, AND WHAT ENSUED

en.hover: Fogg and his companions cross the Indian forests by elephant and encounter a religious procession preparing to sacrifice a young woman.
en.detail: Phileas Fogg, Sir Francis Cromarty, and Passepartout travel by elephant through the wild territory of Bundelcund. Their guide leads them through dense forests and over the Vindhia Mountains to bypass the unfinished railway. During their journey, they hide from a passing procession of Brahmins and fakirs who are leading a young drugged woman to a forced suttee sacrifice, prompting Fogg to propose a rescue since he has time to spare.

schedule.detail: forty-eight hours saved since the beginning of the tour.

tracks.evidence: the guide entered a thick forest... Mr. Fogg patiently waited without a word.
the guide entered a thick forest... Passepartout was all eyes and ears.

chapters.title: IN WHICH PASSEPARTOUT RECEIVES A NEW PROOF THAT FORTUNE FAVORS THE BRAVE

en.hover: Fogg and his companions attempt to rescue Aouda, ultimately succeeding when Passepartout poses as the resuscitated rajah and carries her away.
en.detail: Phileas Fogg, Sir Francis Cromarty, Passepartout, and their Parsee guide plot to rescue the young widow, Aouda, from being burned alive. After an attempt to break into the pagoda fails, they wait until dawn when the sacrifice begins. In a daring move, Passepartout secretly takes the place of the deceased rajah on the pyre, rises as if from the dead, and carries the drugged woman to safety before the guards realize the trick.

tracks.evidence: Phileas Fogg and his companions, mingling in the rear ranks of the crowd, followed
It was Passepartout himself, who had slipped upon the pyre in the midst of the smoke

chapters.title: IN WHICH PHILEAS FOGG DESCENDS THE WHOLE LENGTH OF THE BEAUTIFUL VALLEY OF THE GANGES WITHOUT EVER THINKING OF SEEING IT

en.hover: Fogg, Passepartout, and Sir Francis travel with the rescued Aouda to Allahabad, gift their elephant to the guide, and proceed by train to Calcutta.
en.detail: Following their successful rescue of Aouda, the travellers proceed by elephant to Allahabad, where Fogg generously gifts the valuable animal to their loyal Parsee guide. They board a train, stopping at Benares where Sir Francis departs to rejoin his troops. Continuing rapidly through the Ganges valley, Fogg and Passepartout arrive in Calcutta with Aouda exactly on schedule, ready to board their steamer for Hong Kong.

schedule.detail: neither behind-hand nor ahead of time

tracks.evidence: Calcutta was reached at seven in the morning... so that Phileas Fogg had five hours before him.
Passepartout laughed gaily at his success.

chapters.title: IN WHICH THE BAG OF BANKNOTES DISGORGES SOME THOUSANDS OF POUNDS MORE

en.hover: Fogg and Passepartout are arrested in Calcutta for Passepartout's earlier pagoda desecration, but Fogg pays exorbitant bail so they can catch their steamer.
en.detail: Upon arriving at the station in Calcutta, Fogg, Passepartout, and Aouda are arrested and brought before Judge Obadiah. They discover the detective Fix has orchestrated charges against them for Passepartout's accidental desecration of a Bombay pagoda. Sentenced to prison and heavily fined, Fogg unhesitatingly pays two thousand pounds in bail, allowing the party to rush to the harbour and board the steamer 'Rangoon' for Hong Kong, leaving Fix in despair.

schedule.detail: an hour in advance of time

tracks.evidence: That gentleman took a carriage, and the party were soon landed on one of the quays.
That gentleman took a carriage, and the party were soon landed on one of the quays.
Fix saw them leave the carriage and push off in a boat

chapters.title: IN WHICH FIX DOES NOT SEEM TO UNDERSTAND IN THE LEAST WHAT IS SAID TO HIM

en.hover: Aboard the steamer Rangoon, Aouda grows closer to Fogg while Detective Fix plots to delay Fogg's departure from Hong Kong.
en.detail: The travellers are aboard the steamer Rangoon sailing from Calcutta to Hong Kong. Aouda becomes better acquainted with the politely eccentric Phileas Fogg, feeling deep gratitude for her rescue. Meanwhile, Detective Fix is secretly on board, agonizing over his failure to receive an arrest warrant. He reveals his presence to Passepartout, feigning ignorance of their recent adventures to gather information and plot a way to detain Fogg.

schedule.detail: not a day behind time

tracks.evidence: He visited her regularly each day at certain hours
Passepartout was promenading up and down in the forward part of the steamer.
He had managed to embark on the “Rangoon” at Calcutta... Fix emerged from his cabin and went on deck.

chapters.title: SHOWING WHAT HAPPENED ON THE VOYAGE FROM SINGAPORE TO HONG KONG

en.hover: Passepartout deduces that Fix is a spy sent by the Reform Club, while the travellers stop briefly in Singapore before sailing toward Hong Kong.
en.detail: Passepartout becomes suspicious of Fix's constant presence and concludes he must be a spy hired by the Reform Club to verify Fogg's journey. The steamer Rangoon arrives early in Singapore, allowing Fogg and Aouda a brief carriage ride through the tropical landscape. They depart for Hong Kong, but worsening weather threatens to delay their progress, much to Passepartout's intense frustration.

schedule.detail: gained half a day

tracks.evidence: carried Phileas Fogg and Aouda into the midst of rows of palms
while Passepartout, laughing in his sleeve at Fix’s manœuvres, went about his usual errands.
Fix, who suspected Mr. Fogg’s every movement, followed them cautiously

chapters.title: IN WHICH PHILEAS FOGG, PASSEPARTOUT, AND FIX GO EACH ABOUT HIS BUSINESS

en.hover: A storm delays the Rangoon's arrival in Hong Kong, but Fogg fortuitously catches a delayed steamer and decides to take Aouda to Europe.
en.detail: A severe storm delays the steamer Rangoon, causing it to arrive in Hong Kong twenty-four hours late. Fogg discovers the Yokohama steamer, the 'Carnatic', was also delayed for boiler repairs, saving his schedule. Upon finding that Aouda's cousin Jeejeeh has moved to Europe, Fogg calmly offers to take Aouda with him to Europe, instructing Passepartout to book three cabins on the 'Carnatic'.

schedule.detail: twenty-four hours behind-hand

tracks.evidence: Mr. Fogg, bolder than his servant, did not hesitate to approach the pilot
Passepartout, delighted that the young woman, who was very gracious to him, was going to continue the journey with them, went off at a brisk gait to obey his master’s order.
Fix did not look at the state of things in the same light.

chapters.title: IN WHICH PASSEPARTOUT TAKES A TOO GREAT INTEREST IN HIS MASTER, AND WHAT COMES OF IT

en.hover: In Hong Kong, Fix reveals his true identity to Passepartout and, upon being rebuffed, drugs him with opium to stall Fogg.
en.detail: While exploring Hong Kong, Passepartout discovers that the steamer 'Carnatic' is departing for America that very evening instead of the next morning. He meets Fix, who invites him to a tavern and reveals he is a London detective pursuing Phileas Fogg for a bank robbery. When Passepartout fiercely refuses to betray his master, Fix drugs him with an opium pipe to ensure Fogg misses the early departure of the steamer.

schedule.detail: the steamer leaves that very evening instead of the next morning

tracks.evidence: He accordingly invited his companion into a tavern which caught his eye on the quay.
He accordingly invited his companion into a tavern which caught his eye on the quay.

chapters.title: IN WHICH FIX COMES FACE TO FACE WITH PHILEAS FOGG

en.hover: Fogg discovers the Carnatic sailed early without them. Unfazed, he charters the Tankadere to take his party and a secretly thwarted Fix to Shanghai.
en.detail: Unaware of Passepartout's drug-induced stupor, Fogg and Aouda arrive at the quay only to discover the Carnatic has sailed early. Undeterred by the setback, Fogg searches the docks and charters a small pilot-boat, the Tankadere, captained by John Bunsby, to reach Shanghai in time to catch the Pacific steamer. After leaving funds with the police to search for his missing servant, Fogg, Aouda, and a secretly disappointed Fix set sail.

schedule.detail: left Hong Kong twelve hours before the stated time

tracks.evidence: quietly escorting Aouda about the streets of the English quarter
It was Fix, who, bowing, addressed Mr. Fogg: “Were you not, like me, sir, a passenger by the ‘Rangoon,’ which arrived yesterday?”

chapters.title: IN WHICH THE MASTER OF THE "TANKADERE" RUNS GREAT RISK OF LOSING A REWARD OF TWO HUNDRED POUNDS

en.hover: Phileas Fogg, Aouda, and Fix brave a violent typhoon aboard the pilot-boat Tankadere, racing to reach Shanghai to catch the Yokohama steamer.
en.detail: Determined to catch the Yokohama steamer, Phileas Fogg charters the small pilot-boat Tankadere to take him, Aouda, and Fix from Hong Kong to Shanghai. En route, they endure a terrifying typhoon but hold their course, reaching the Shanghai River just as the American steamer is departing. In a final bid to catch it, Fogg orders the pilot to fire a distress cannon.

schedule.detail: hoping to reach Yokohama without recording any delay

tracks.evidence: Phileas Fogg, with body erect and legs wide apart, standing like a sailor, gazed without staggering at the swelling waters.
Fix, seated in the bow, gave himself up to meditation.

chapters.title: IN WHICH PASSEPARTOUT FINDS OUT THAT, EVEN AT THE ANTIPODES, IT IS CONVENIENT TO HAVE SOME MONEY IN ONE'S POCKET

en.hover: Passepartout wakes up on the Carnatic bound for Japan, realizes he left Fogg behind, and arrives in Yokohama penniless and hungry.
en.detail: Awaking from his opium-induced stupor aboard the Carnatic, Passepartout discovers that Phileas Fogg and Aouda missed the ship because he failed to inform them of its early departure. Arriving in Yokohama, Japan, he finds himself alone with no money. He wanders the exotic streets of the European and Japanese quarters, growing increasingly hungry as night falls.

schedule.detail: Fogg missed the steamer, throwing his schedule into doubt.

tracks.evidence: Passepartout went timidly ashore on this so curious territory of the Sons of the Sun. He had nothing better to do than, taking chance for his guide, to wander aimlessly through the streets of Yokohama.

chapters.title: IN WHICH PASSEPARTOUT'S NOSE BECOMES OUTRAGEOUSLY LONG

en.hover: Penniless in Japan, Passepartout joins an acrobatic troupe. During a performance, he spots Phileas Fogg and Aouda, reuniting to board the American steamer.
en.detail: Stranded without money, Passepartout trades his clothes for Japanese garments to afford a small meal. To secure passage across the Pacific, he takes a job in the Honourable William Batulcar's acrobatic troupe as a base for a human pyramid. While performing, he spots Fogg and Aouda in the audience, breaking the formation to rush to them. After Fogg pays for the damages, they all board the American steamer together.

schedule.detail: Departing exactly on time at half-past six

tracks.evidence: He followed the clown, and soon found himself once more in the Japanese quarter.

chapters.title: DURING WHICH MR. FOGG AND PARTY CROSS THE PACIFIC OCEAN

en.hover: Phileas Fogg reunites with Passepartout in Yokohama, and the entire party boards the steamer General Grant to cross the Pacific.
en.detail: After boarding the Yokohama steamer off the coast of Shanghai, Fogg, Aouda, and Fix arrive in Yokohama. There, Fogg discovers Passepartout working in a theatre troupe. Reunited and re-clothed, they board the General Grant to cross the Pacific to San Francisco. During the voyage, Fix and Passepartout agree to a truce, and the ship arrives exactly on schedule.

schedule.detail: neither gained nor lost a single day

tracks.evidence: The steamer which was about to depart from Yokohama to San Francisco belonged to the Pacific Mail Steamship Company
On that very day, however, he met Passepartout face to face on the forward deck.
His course decided on, he went on board the “General Grant,” and was there when Mr. Fogg and Aouda arrived.

chapters.title: IN WHICH A SLIGHT GLIMPSE IS HAD OF SAN FRANCISCO

en.hover: Fogg and his companions explore San Francisco, where they accidentally get caught in a violent election riot before catching their train to New York.
en.detail: Phileas Fogg, Aouda, and Passepartout arrive in San Francisco. While Fogg and Aouda explore the city and head to the English consulate with Fix, they find themselves caught in the middle of a violent street brawl over the election of a justice of the peace. Fogg is confronted by a belligerent American, Colonel Stamp Proctor, before the party boards the evening train for New York.

schedule.detail: He has an entire day to spend in San Francisco.

tracks.evidence: At a quarter before six the travellers reached the station
At a quarter before six the travellers reached the station
At a quarter before six the travellers reached the station

chapters.title: IN WHICH PHILEAS FOGG AND PARTY TRAVEL BY THE PACIFIC RAILROAD

en.hover: Phileas Fogg and his companions begin their train journey across America, facing a lengthy delay when a massive herd of buffalo crosses the tracks.
en.detail: The travelers depart Oakland on the Pacific Railroad, crossing California and entering Nevada. The journey provides stunning views of the Sierra Nevada mountains and comfortable sleeping arrangements in a converted car. However, their progress is interrupted in Nevada by a massive herd of buffalo blocking the tracks for three hours, much to Passepartout's frustration, before they continue into Utah.

schedule.detail: Delayed three hours by buffaloes, expecting to regain the lost time by greater speed.

tracks.evidence: Having breakfasted, Mr. Fogg and his companions resumed their places in the car
Passepartout found himself beside the detective; but he did not talk to him.
Fix’s manner had not changed; but Passepartout was very reserved

chapters.title: IN WHICH PASSEPARTOUT UNDERGOES, AT A SPEED OF TWENTY MILES AN HOUR, A COURSE OF MORMON HISTORY

en.hover: A Mormon missionary lectures on the train as they approach Utah; later, the group briefly visits Salt Lake City.
en.detail: As the train travels towards the Great Salt Lake, a Mormon missionary, Elder William Hitch, delivers a lecture on Mormon history in one of the cars, with Passepartout eventually becoming his only listener. The train arrives in Ogden, allowing Fogg and his party time to visit Salt Lake City via a branch line before returning to the train. Just as they depart, a fleeing Mormon boards the train to escape his single, overbearing wife.

schedule.detail: The train stopped at Ogden for 6 hours, allowing a side trip to Salt Lake City.

tracks.evidence: Mr. Fogg and his party had time to pay a visit to Salt Lake City... The travellers, then, were promenading, at three o’clock, about the streets
Passepartout could not behold without a certain fright these women
Neither Mr. Fogg nor Fix cared to attend. ... At four the party found themselves again at the station

chapters.title: IN WHICH PASSEPARTOUT DOES NOT SUCCEED IN MAKING ANYBODY LISTEN TO REASON

en.hover: The train encounters a ruined suspension bridge, and the engineer proposes jumping it at full speed, much to Passepartout's alarm.
en.detail: As the train continues across the Rocky Mountains, Aouda spots Colonel Proctor on board, and the group distracts Fogg with whist to prevent a duel. The journey is halted by a severely damaged suspension bridge over Medicine Bow rapids. Instead of the passengers crossing safely on foot first—as Passepartout vainly attempts to suggest—the engineer successfully drives the entire train across at maximum speed just as the bridge collapses behind them.

schedule.detail: Delay is averted by the train jumping the broken bridge.

tracks.evidence: At ten o’clock at night the train stopped at Fort Bridger station
At ten o’clock at night the train stopped at Fort Bridger station
At ten o’clock at night the train stopped at Fort Bridger station

chapters.title: IN WHICH CERTAIN INCIDENTS ARE NARRATED WHICH ARE ONLY TO BE MET WITH ON AMERICAN RAILROADS

en.hover: Colonel Proctor forces Fogg into a duel aboard the train, but a sudden attack by Sioux warriors interrupts them.
en.detail: As the train continues its journey across the American West, Colonel Proctor interrupts Fogg's whist game and demands a duel. Unable to stop at Plum Creek, they prepare to fight in the rear car. Before they can duel, a band of Sioux attacks the train. Passepartout heroically uncouples the cars to stop the train near Fort Kearney, but goes missing in the aftermath.

schedule.detail: Phileas Fogg was not as yet behind-hand.

tracks.evidence: “It shall be stopped,” said Phileas Fogg, preparing to rush from the car.
There, suspended by one hand between the baggage-car and the tender, with the other he loosened the safety chains
Fix got up, and, going to Colonel Proctor said, “You forget that it is I with whom you have to deal, sir

chapters.title: IN WHICH PHILEAS FOGG SIMPLY DOES HIS DUTY

en.hover: Fogg sacrifices his schedule to rescue Passepartout from the Sioux, missing his train but successfully returning with his servant.
en.detail: Discovering Passepartout missing after the Sioux attack, Fogg hires thirty soldiers from Fort Kearney to rescue him, knowing the delay will likely cost him his wager. While he is gone, the runaway locomotive returns, and the train departs for Omaha without Fogg, Aouda, or Fix. Fogg returns the next morning, having successfully rescued Passepartout, only to find the train gone.

schedule.detail: Missed the train, which left three hours late, ensuring he will miss the New York steamer.

chapters.title: IN WHICH FIX, THE DETECTIVE, CONSIDERABLY FURTHERS THE INTERESTS OF PHILEAS FOGG

en.hover: Fogg hires a wind-powered sledge to race to Omaha, catching trains to New York only to miss his Liverpool steamer by minutes.
en.detail: Stranded and twenty hours behind schedule, Fogg accepts Fix's suggestion to hire a wind-powered sledge driven by an American named Mudge. The sledge races across the frozen plains to Omaha, where the party boards a series of trains to Chicago and then New York. Despite their rapid transit across the country, they arrive at the New York pier just 45 minutes after their steamer has sailed for Liverpool.

transport.vessel: Pittsburgh, Fort Wayne, and Chicago Railway

schedule.detail: Despite racing across the country, they missed the steamer to Liverpool by 45 minutes.

tracks.evidence: A train was ready to start when Mr. Fogg and his party reached the station, and they only had time to get into the cars.
A train was ready to start when Mr. Fogg and his party reached the station, and they only had time to get into the cars.
A train was ready to start when Mr. Fogg and his party reached the station, and they only had time to get into the cars.

chapters.title: IN WHICH PHILEAS FOGG ENGAGES IN A DIRECT STRUGGLE WITH BAD FORTUNE

en.hover: Phileas Fogg searches the New York docks for a ship to cross the Atlantic and hires the Henrietta to sail to Bordeaux.
en.detail: Having missed the steamer for Liverpool, Phileas Fogg and his companions secure lodging in New York. The following day, Fogg scours the docks for a departing vessel and meets Captain Andrew Speedy of the Henrietta. When Speedy steadfastly refuses to sail to Liverpool, Fogg offers him two thousand dollars per passenger to take them to Bordeaux, securing their passage just in time.

schedule.detail: could not cross the Atlantic in time to save the wager

tracks.evidence: He seemed about to give up all hope, when he espied, anchored at the Battery
after giving Passepartout instructions to await his return
hurry to the St. Nicholas, and return with Aouda, Passepartout, and even the inseparable Fix... They were on board when the “Henrietta” made ready to weigh anchor.

chapters.title: IN WHICH PHILEAS FOGG SHOWS HIMSELF EQUAL TO THE OCCASION

en.hover: Phileas Fogg takes over the Henrietta, burns its wooden parts for fuel, reaches Ireland, and is arrested upon arriving in Liverpool.
en.detail: Phileas Fogg bribes the crew of the Henrietta to lock up Captain Speedy and sail toward Liverpool. When the coal supply runs low, Fogg buys the ship at a premium and burns its wooden fixtures to keep the steam going. Reaching Ireland, Fogg's party takes a train to Dublin and a fast steamer to Liverpool, only for Fix to finally arrest Fogg just as they disembark.

schedule.detail: He was only six hours distant from London.

tracks.evidence: Phileas Fogg at last disembarked on the Liverpool quay, at twenty minutes before twelve, 21st December.
As for Passepartout, he thought Mr. Fogg’s manœuvre simply glorious.
But at this moment Fix came up, put his hand upon Mr. Fogg’s shoulder, and, showing his warrant, said, “You are really Phileas Fogg?”

chapters.title: IN WHICH PHILEAS FOGG AT LAST REACHES LONDON

en.hover: Phileas Fogg is held in the Liverpool Custom House but is released when the real robber is caught, chartering a train to London too late.
en.detail: Phileas Fogg is imprisoned in the Liverpool Custom House by Detective Fix, effectively ruining his chances of winning the wager. Passepartout is devastated, blaming himself for not warning Fogg about Fix's true motives. Fix suddenly returns with news that the real bank robber was caught three days prior. A freed Fogg knocks Fix down and charters a special train to London, but arrives five minutes late.

schedule.detail: behind-hand five minutes

tracks.evidence: at last set out towards London with Aouda and his faithful servant.
at last set out towards London with Aouda and his faithful servant.
The door swung open, and he saw Passepartout, Aouda, and Fix, who hurried towards him.

chapters.title: IN WHICH PHILEAS FOGG DOES NOT HAVE TO REPEAT HIS ORDERS TO PASSEPARTOUT TWICE

en.hover: Believing himself ruined, Phileas Fogg returns home, where a devastated Aouda unexpectedly proposes marriage to him, which he joyfully accepts.
en.detail: Phileas Fogg returns to his house on Saville Row, believing he has lost his wager and his fortune. He locks himself away to settle his affairs, while a guilt-ridden Passepartout keeps watch. During an evening conversation, Fogg apologizes to Aouda for his ruin; in response, she proposes marriage to him, and he happily accepts, sending Passepartout for a clergyman.

en.hover: As the deadline for the wager approaches, Fogg's friends wait at the Reform Club until he dramatically appears at the final second.
en.detail: Following the arrest of the real bank robber, James Strand, public opinion in London swings entirely back in Phileas Fogg's favor. On the evening the wager is set to expire, his five friends anxiously wait in the Reform Club while a massive crowd gathers outside. Having received no news, the men count down the final seconds of the wager, only for Fogg to suddenly enter the room right on time.

tracks.evidence: At the fifty-seventh second the door of the saloon opened; and the pendulum had not beat the sixtieth second when Phileas Fogg appeared

chapters.title: IN WHICH IT IS SHOWN THAT PHILEAS FOGG GAINED NOTHING BY HIS TOUR AROUND THE WORLD, UNLESS IT WERE HAPPINESS

en.hover: Fogg learns he miscounted a day, rushes to the Reform Club in time to win his wager, and marries Aouda.
en.detail: Passepartout discovers that it is actually Saturday, not Sunday, and drags Fogg to the Reform Club, where Fogg arrives with minutes to spare and wins his twenty-thousand-pound wager. The chapter explains that by travelling constantly eastward Fogg unknowingly gained a full day, seeing the sun cross the meridian eighty times to London's seventy-nine. Though his winnings barely exceed his expenses, Fogg marries Aouda, whose suggestion of marriage had prompted the errand that revealed his error. In the end his real gain from the journey is happiness, not money.
